name: Wall Calf Stretch
description: The wall calf stretch uses a wall for support and targets the gastrocnemius with the knee straight and the soleus with the knee bent. With the knee straight, the gastrocnemius — which crosses the knee — is placed on maximal tension as the heel is pressed toward the floor and the foot dorsiflexed. The bent-knee version specifically isolates the soleus, which does not cross the knee joint.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a wall at arm's length. Place both hands on the wall for support.
execution.setup_instructions: Stand near a solid wall. No equipment needed.
steps: Step 1: Place both hands on the wall and step one foot back approximately 60–90 cm.
Step 2: Keep the rear knee straight and press the rear heel firmly into the floor.
Step 3: Lean gently into the wall by bending the front knee, dorsiflexing the rear ankle.
Step 4: Hold until a stretch is felt in the calf of the rear leg — 30–60 seconds.
Step 5: To target the soleus, slightly bend the rear knee while keeping the heel down. Hold again.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe naturally and steadily throughout the hold.
common_mistakes: Lifting the heel of the rear foot off the floor, which eliminates the stretch
Rotating the rear foot outward rather than keeping it straight
Not stepping back far enough to feel the stretch
safety_considerations: Avoid this stretch during acute Achilles tendon injury — consult a clinician first
Ensure the wall can support body weight without slipping
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lean into the wall until a noticeable but comfortable calf stretch is felt. The rear heel must remain on the floor.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 30–60 seconds straight-leg for gastrocnemius, 30–60 seconds bent-knee for soleus. 2–3 rounds.
coaching_cues: Press the heel through the floor — the stretch comes from the floor pushing back
Keep the rear foot pointing straight ahead
Bend the rear knee slightly to shift the stretch from the gastrocnemius to the soleus
